content.text:
No — `translate-guides.ts` doesn't need any additions. It already has the same `defaultVerbatim: { allow: ["en*"] }` policy as every other workflow (in [translate-guides.ts](docs/scripts/translate-guides.ts#L45)). The extra `verbatimSources` set you see in [translate-chrome.ts](docs/scripts/translate-chrome.ts#L27-L34) is a different mechanism, for a different problem:

- `verbatimSources` exempts specific short `kind: "text"` units (individual UI strings) whose entire content is a literal token — a status code, "Canvas", a CSS keyword — from the "identical to source, must be untranslated" guard, because those exact strings are legitimately unchanged in every locale.
- Guide units are `kind: "markdown"` — whole files, not short tokens — so a `verbatimSources` entry would require the *entire page's* content to exactly match a listed literal string, which isn't applicable here.
- In-document protection (fenced code blocks, inline code, package names) is handled independently inside `adapter.translateMarkdown` itself via masking (see `api-translation.ts`'s `preserveMarkdownSensitiveBlocks`/`packages`/`brackets` masking), not through the `verbatimSources`/`defaultVerbatim` options at all.

So the existing `{ locale, defaultVerbatim: { allow: ["en*"] } }` is the correct and sufficient policy for guides.
